blocks.text: Britain has a king and is a democracy. Saudi Arabia has a king and is not. Nigeria has had neither king nor democracy for long stretches of its history — for almost thirty of its first forty years it was governed by soldiers. Forms of government are best learned by asking one question: who holds the final say?

blocks.markdown:
A **monarchy** is a system in which the headship of state is hereditary and held for life. Everything then turns on how much power the monarch actually exercises.

In an **absolute monarchy** the monarch personally holds executive, legislative and often judicial power. He is not bound by an elected legislature, and there is no constitution he cannot alter. Saudi Arabia, Oman, Brunei and Eswatini are modern examples.

In a **constitutional monarchy** the monarch is a ceremonial head of state whose powers are limited by a constitution, while real executive power belongs to an elected Prime Minister and Cabinet. The United Kingdom, Japan, Spain, Sweden, Morocco and Lesotho are examples. Nigeria itself was a constitutional monarchy from independence on 1 October 1960 until it became a republic on 1 October 1963, with Queen Elizabeth II as Head of State represented in Nigeria by the Governor-General.

blocks.title: Autocracy and dictatorship
blocks.text: An autocracy is any system in which one person exercises unlimited power without effective legal or popular restraint. A dictatorship is an autocracy in which that power was usually seized rather than inherited. The distinguishing marks are the absence of free elections, the suppression of opposition and the fusion of all powers in one hand.

blocks.markdown:
### Effects of military rule on Nigeria

Military governments centralised a federation: because command flows downwards in an army, states became administrative units taking orders from Lagos and later Abuja, and revenue was concentrated at the centre. Almost every change in Nigeria's structure was made by soldiers — twelve states in 1967, nineteen states and the creation of the Federal Capital Territory in 1976, twenty-one in 1987, thirty in 1991 and thirty-six in 1996.

The record is genuinely mixed. Military regimes built national institutions such as the National Youth Service Corps, established in 1973, and prosecuted large infrastructure programmes during the oil boom. Against that stand the suspension of fundamental rights, detention without trial, the execution of critics, the annulment of the presidential election of 12 June 1993, and a deep culture of impunity and corruption whose effects outlasted the regimes themselves.

blocks.title: Classifying a regime from its features
blocks.prompt: A country is governed by a council of eleven senior officers. The constitution is suspended, decrees replace statutes, all parties are banned, the head of state appoints provincial administrators, and the courts may not question any decree. Classify this government precisely and justify each element of your answer.

steps.text: Count the rulers. Eleven officers, not one person and not the whole people, so the government is in the hands of a small group — an oligarchy in the broad sense.
Identify the group's nature. They are serving military officers who took power by coup, so the precise label is a military regime or military oligarchy.
Check the legislative method. Rule by decree with the constitution suspended shows there is no separation of powers: the council makes and executes law together.
Check the treatment of opposition and courts. A ban on parties and ouster clauses removing judicial review mark the regime as autocratic, not merely non-elected.
State the conclusion with its evidence: a military oligarchy exercising autocratic power, identified by the suspended constitution, rule by decree, banned parties, fused powers and ousted courts.

blocks.answer: A military regime — an autocratic oligarchy of officers — evidenced by the suspended constitution, rule by decree, banned parties, fusion of powers and exclusion of judicial review

blocks.title: The trap in monarchy questions
blocks.text: Never write that a monarchy is undemocratic. Say instead that an ABSOLUTE monarchy is undemocratic while a CONSTITUTIONAL monarchy is compatible with democracy, and name Britain as your evidence. That single distinction separates a strong answer from an average one.

points: A monarchy has a hereditary head of state holding office for life.
An absolute monarch exercises real, unrestrained power; a constitutional monarch is a ceremonial figure limited by the constitution.
Nigeria was a constitutional monarchy from 1 October 1960 until it became a republic on 1 October 1963.
Aristocracy is rule by a privileged class, oligarchy rule by a small group, theocracy rule by religious leaders and totalitarianism total state control.
Military rule suspends the constitution, governs by decree, bans parties and fuses the powers of government.
Nigeria was under military rule from 1966 to 1979 and from 1983 to 1999, and every change in the number of states was made by a military government.
